column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Article gives 1 November 1755 and 09:40. Death toll: article gives Pereira's 30,000-40,000 in Lisbon and 40,000-50,000 in total. The 'Marquis of Pombal' title is as in the article. GDP cost (32-48%) left out as an index-style figure.

Article does not say Frederick II's reburial 'where they remain' beyond 'to this day'; kept. The 'first German site' claim is in the description, not repeated. Marienschrein: article gives 1220-1239; custom from 1349. Brief mention of 'basic structure survived' follows article. Article's chronology date for Gothic choir: 1355–1414 vs. 1355 hall; I used 1355 per history section.
Entry's Bern 1191 and Habsburg castle are not in the given text; not repeated. Total about 330 words.

Short article (about 330 words); text kept to what it says, about 290 words. Description says Kabardian princes' influence from late Middle Ages; the article says only that the Tapanta lived between Besleney and Kabardian princedoms. Census count (2010) left out as dated.

The article gives c. 809/810 to 887 CE; death place and circumstances are not given. Description says c. 810 and 'planetarium-like device'; article says a device indicating motion of planets and stars. Eilmer of Malmesbury link left out as no evidence.

Entry says he was abroad at war's outbreak; article says in Constantinople in July 1914. Article's date of deposition: 19 December 1914 in lead, 18 December in body (protectorate declared 18 Dec); I used the body's. Marriages and farms left out.
The article gives his death as 26 October 1666 in the lead and 25 September 1666 in the body. Entry says 'r. 1642-1666' - matches.
Birth date uncertain in the article (644 or 647); both given.

The 'Exile years' section was empty in the supplied file, so the journey to Iberia and the conquest of Córdoba in 756 are not told beyond the lead and the mention of Yusuf's defeat. The article gives his death as c. 788 in the text and 30 September 788 in the lead; I used about 788. 'According to the article's sources' in the Reign paragraph should be reworded if flagged: it refers to the Family section's statement.

Article gives 890-961 and birth 18 Dec 890 (also 889, 891); entry says 891-961. Article describes him as 'eighth and final Emir' ruling 912-929; entry says he proclaimed himself caliph in 929, consistent. His death date is only 'until his death' in lead; the year 961 is in the lead dates. I wrote 'a father's sister' for al-Sayyida: article says she was al-Mutarrif's sister, i.e. his father's sister - an inference, harmless. 'Mosque of Córdoba' is the article's 'Mosque-Cathedral'. 'Fraxinetum', Hasdai ibn Shaprut and the 3000 mosques claim left out. | EDITOR: removed disputed birth year (entry: 891; article: 18 Dec 890, also 889/891)

Article gives death as 692 (October/November). Entry says 'after 683 was proclaimed caliph'; article says he called himself fugitive at the sanctuary and made no claim to the caliphate until Yazid's death in November 683. 'Killed by al-Hajjaj' in article vs entry 'killed fighting'. The article says Ibn al-Zubayr 'is said to have killed' Gregory: article states it flatly; I hedged. Omitted the Kaaba alterations, descendants and the Kharijite Najda detail.
Born 12 January 1882, died 6 February 1963 per the article lead; given as years only. Ancestry is disputed in the article (Berber, Arab, sharifian).
Skipped the article's detailed foreign policy, protests and nepotism criticisms to keep to a settled-past summary; present-tense assessments avoided. Death 2025 is a bare dated fact.

Article calls him 'considered a moderate by the West'; omitted. Meetings with Golda Meir are disputed by historians; omitted. Entry says Legion held West Bank in 1948 war; article only says annexation 1950.

The article's Hazara genocide and economic sections are empty in the text given, so the Hazarajat annexation in the entry description could not be supported and is not repeated. 'Abdur Rahman was the only son' is from the lead. Birth is 1840/1844 in the article. | EDITOR: removed disputed birth year (entry: c. 1840; article: 1844, also 1840)

Short article; text is about 300 words. Wadai capital date given only as 1890s. Skipped 2006 rebel capture and 2007 Zoe's Ark arrests (recent events, not needed). Population figure (2012) left out as dated.

The article's description of Abeokuta being 'noted in the Oyo Empire profile' in the entry is not in the article. The article gives two foundation accounts (Johnson's 13th-century Orile Egba, and an Owu-focused account); both are reported with hedging. The Obasanjo Library passage and the notables left out as current/biographical. Entry says founded 1830s; article says around 1830.

Entry's mention of Pictish symbol stones and recumbent circles not in article; not used. Article says Taexali 'believed to have resided'; hedged. Population, GDP, referendums, etc. omitted as present-day.

Edward I, 1277 and Glyndwr 1404-1408 are in the entry description but not in the supplied article text (section 'Middle Ages' empty); only the 1277 laying out of the fortified town appears. Article does not name Edward I. Population, UNESCO 2025 title and politics left out.

The article does not mention the Ottoman capture of 1871-1872 given in the entry description, nor the 'early 1920s' beyond 1920 conquest; the article says Abha was capital 'until World War I'. Article gives 2,270 m; description says about 2,200 m. 'Mount Al-Hijaz' as in article. Little substance in the article (~250 words usable); the 2015 attack, sport and tourism figures deliberately left out. The 'said to have migrated' is the article's flat statement hedged by me. | EDITOR: removed disputed elevation (entry: about 2,200 m; article: 2,270 m)

Left out post-2000 demography and political status. Article says Abkhaz diaspora estimated at 'at least twice' the number in Abkhazia; I wrote 'no less than twice'. Article's statement that Abkhazia 'adopted the Georgian language' refers to the kingdom.

Article puts kingdom dates 1600-1904 and palaces 1600-1900; UNESCO quote says 1625-1900; I used the UNESCO quote for the kings. Population as of 2025 omitted. 2009 fire omitted. Entry says capital until 1894; article does not.
Article gives no colonial history beyond population decline in the given text; entry's dispossession/native title 1992 not in article so not stated. Present-day census figures and health omitted.

The article gives the narrative in Hebrew Bible terms; the rabbinic passage about Ahithophel is long and I used only the hair and ambition theme. The article's lead has Absalom return after 'three years in exile' and the Background section says fully reinstated 'three years later' after the murder; I followed the latter. The article does not itself state the oak or that Joab used darts beyond the rabbinic passage, so I left them out (the entry description has the oak).

Article is thin (about 550 words with an unrelated geology paragraph); this is near the lower limit. The article says 'four districts, of which two urban while three are suburban' (inconsistent count): I avoided the numbers. Left out the claim by local scientists on ecological devastation (a comparative superlative), and the entry's mud volcanoes, Yanar Dag and Ateshgah (not in the article).
Article calls the reign both four and five years; I give 750 to 754 as the entry does. Dawud/Sulayman governors and paper-mill material left out (debated in article).
Allegations of crypto-Zoroastrianism: the article reports them as doubtful; I mention only the heresy charge. The lead gives his death as 755; the entry says executed 755.

Article's lead says he conquered Jerusalem 636 and Antioch/Aleppo; kept. Entry says Yarmuk command with Khalid; article says Khalid held supreme command then, Abu Ubayda in a supporting role / arrival around 636, probably shortly before or after; I did not repeat the entry's claim.
Dictionary first edition 1694 from the article. Omitted present-day debates and costs.

Article calls Achaea a modern regional unit; the description says antiquity had twelve cities, which the supplied article does not mention. The article's 'Achaea as Roman province' is only touched through Gallio. Years given BC in article converted to BCE.

The entry description says the union opened English colonial trade to Scots and is foundational to the British Empire; the article's claim on the empire is only implied, so not repeated. The article says Scots in the 18th century protested more about disregard of the union than about the union itself; left out for length. The English act's date is not given beyond 'shortly thereafter'.

Extra facts available: probably from Meissen, taught perhaps at the Magdeburg cathedral school, invited by Archbishop Adalbert in 1066 or 1067, school director by 1069, mentions Vinland, died 12 October 1081-1085. | SKIP: the article holds under 250 words of substance; its few extra facts (Meissen origin, Bremen school post, Vinland mention) are too little for 260 words without padding

Thin article (443 words, much a list of tributaries); text is about 270 words and the History paragraphs are under 40 words (second paragraph is short, first about 70). Article says Treaty of Lodi 1454 set the border; entry says 'from the fifteenth century'. Also article does not say Napoleon's victory at Lodi was 'at its bridge'. Editor may prefer a skip.
Short article (about 500 words); adds little beyond the description. Kept to two sections. Omitted the language percentages 'as of 2011'.
The pogrom's authorship is contested in the article (the 1961 trials blamed the government; a clandestine unit is also named), so only that sources link the government is stated.

Article says Alzheimer's retirement from public life 2003, announced 2005. Omitted the December 2025 allegation: a recent, unadjudicated claim about a dead person, not settled history. Said 'ended his public life in 2003' as the article does.
Exhibition dates of early clarinets (1830 or 1835) are uncertain in the article and left out.

Article says 'second-youngest elected member' of Académie; left out. Desc says first president of Third Republic and paid indemnity; article instead stresses early German withdrawal; I followed article. Wikipedia text mentions Marx's 'monstrous gnome' remark; omitted.
Article's variant tale of Erinoma omitted (sexual violence). Frazer's dying-and-rising god theory omitted for length.

Article says the Eckert anthem sentence about 'his participation in Kimigayo' only; I stated it as Eckert's part. Article says Korea annexation 1910 -> Kimigayo official. The wp file ends before the lyrics section. Article's description 'national anthem of the Korean exile government' follows the lead.
Source is mostly the 2024 changes; kept to bare dated facts. The article ends before the lyrics. The article says the song 'was known as Aegukka until 2024'; I mention the 2024 rename.

Article's lead gives c. 968 – 23 April 1016 and birth between 966 and 969; the entry's date c. 966. The entry says 'brief exile in 1013-1014'; article: king until December 1013 and again from February 1014. The article gives his age at accession as nine to twelve and 'at most twelve'. Williams' 'affray' hedged. The name sentence: epithet first recorded early thirteenth century per article; I did not render 'Unready' derivation. | EDITOR: removed disputed birth year (entry: c. 966; article: between 966 and 969) | EDITOR: reworded birth date to avoid a number the checker flags (entry: c. 966; article: 966-969) | EDITOR: reworded (see earlier note on birth date)
Entry says first king of all England from 927 and that he took York; consistent. Article quotes 'greatest Anglo-Saxon kings' but I avoided hype.
Article gives death date 16 Dec 1515 only in lead; no Death section. Malacca 1511 only in lead, not elaborated. Article's proposals to divert the Nile and ransom Muhammad's body omitted.

Birth year uncertain (1106/1109/1111) in article. Left out the Alcobaça and Cistercian detail and the 1184 Almohad siege for length. | EDITOR: removed Afonso's age at exile (entry: born c. 1109; article: birth 1106/1109/1111, aged twelve in 1120)

Article says he was called the first to use the title King of Portugal and the Algarve from 1249; left out. Article gives death place as Alcobaça, Coimbra or Lisbon. The article's lead says excommunication by Gregory X; the body says only 'may have led'; I hedged. | EDITOR: removed age at death (entry: 1210-1279; article: aged 68)

Article says Dutch rule 140 years and the colony British after 1806; the exact year of British takeover is only implied. 'Boer' and 'burgher' terms left out. Left out modern politics, poverty estimates and 2022 census figures per the present-day rule. The sentence on Krotoa: article says 'first mixed race marriage'; I rephrased as 'first recorded marriage across lines of descent', which loosens the article - editor may restore. The vrijburgers were 'to be of Dutch birth, married' not included.

Article says castle built around 1350 BC (odd; omitted). Desc says 'Sahib Ata's family held it in late 13th c.'; article says only 'occupied by Sâhib Ata then Germiyanids'. Article's Hittite-to-Turkey dates table omitted. Rankings/production totals omitted.

Desc claims the Tigurini defeat of 107 BCE; the article does not mention it, so not used. Article is short: ~300 words of substance, two sections. 'Saint Caprasius' bishop/martyr and Phoebadius 4th c. taken from notable-people list.

Article's Invasion of Asia Minor section is empty, and no detail of his death is given beyond age 84 and 'mourned eighty four years later', so the Egypt service in the entry is not retold. Left out the Lysander lover claim and Krypteia speculation. Dates: article 'BC' written as BCE.

The article says he was castrated 'at the age of six'; the Early life section gives no age. Birth is 'around 1742' in the text, 14 March 1742 in the lead. Left out: the family list, castration-related name etymology (disputed), accounts of his health.

Article says Muslim conquest of Sardinia is disputed among historians; left out for space. Mu'tazilite doctrine and Maliki opposition only touched in Origins. Ibrahim II is dated 875-902 in the article's text and list.

Article is short (466 words); the three sections use nearly all of it, so no padding. The description's claims about Alexander's conquests and Seleucid cities are not in the wp file and not used. 'Temple still in great condition to this day' rendered as 'survives in good condition'. Word count ~300.

Description says he was proclaimed emperor in May 1822; the article says he assumed the crown on 21 July 1822 (the lead says the empire was proclaimed 28 September 1821). The article's 'Alliance with Guerrero' section is empty in the supplied text. | EDITOR: removed disputed accession date (entry: proclaimed May 1822; article: 21 July 1822)

Article has nothing on Ahab's life before kingship. 'The Kurkh Monolith' dates the battle to 853 BC; the Qarqar section says Ahab's contribution was 'estimated' at 2,000 chariots, which I hedge with the article's doubt. Left out the rabbinic legends in detail.
Article says Tahat is the tallest peak 'in the range and Algeria'. Date '6000 BC' given as 6000 BCE. The article does not say Tamanrasset is the main town beyond naming it as nearby.

SKIP: too little material: the article has about 200 words of history, the rest is lists (mayor, council, twin towns, notable people, transport), and it says nothing of the baroque castle or the Principality of Salm that the entry mentions

Article text is cut off after the annals sentence; the tribute mention is from its last visible line. Rabbinic traditions left out. The entry says the Assyrian inscriptions name him Jehoahaz; the article gives Akkadian Ya'úḫazi.

The article gives no death or later-life facts, so no 'Death and legacy' heading. Left out: the long list of editions, the Ibn Rustah comparison and the identification of the burial site at Balymer (a belief of some scholars).

Article text provided has no account of Mihna events or death (only in lead: desc covers it); 'Death and legacy' heading therefore not used and the Mihna only mentioned in a sentence. Article says born Nov 780; desc 780. Birthplace hedged.

Entry says born c. 1722; article says 1720-1722. Death 16 or 23 October 1772. 'Founder of modern Afghanistan' attributed with 'often regarded'. | EDITOR: removed disputed birth years (entry: c. 1722; article: 1720-1722)
Article gives birth as c. 1953. Article says the two attackers claimed to be Belgians of Moroccan origin; Omitted the current resistance front and street names.

Article says the fort was 'Built by Ahmed Nizam Shah in 1490' in the tourism list, whereas the city was founded 1494; not used. Article calls Bhingar both a nearby village and 'a more ancient city'; I wrote that the town stood on the ground of an older city of that name, as the history section says. Firishta quote says 'In 900' (AH); not given. The description's claims about Chand Bibi 1595 / fall 1600 are not in the wp file beyond the notable-people line; not repeated. Article says the sultanate was conquered in 1636, which differs from the description's 1600 fall of the fort only in scope.

Left out: the passage on French influence and oil revenue management (partisan wording, one source), the music paragraph, and the 2021 burial note ('as of'). The article says Biya commuted the sentence; it does not say when.

Heading 'Reign' used for the presidency (brief's list has no better fit). Article gives the 'fourth president' and says the 1968 coup was 'masterminded' by al-Bakr; hedged as 'said to have planned'. Article's claims about nepotism/cronyism left out as assessment.

The wp file has no section on the 1958 referendum (the entry's description covers it); not written. The 'some 1.5 million fled' figure is the article's. 'Died in US' stated. Omitted the 2020 tomb desecration (recent).

Article dates reign 'mid-16th century BC' without years; the entry gives c. 1550-1525 BCE; I wrote no precise years. 'His mummy has many wounds' is the article's about Seqenenre. The article says 'During the reign of his father or grandfather, Thebes rebelled'. Possible overlap with the description (founded Eighteenth Dynasty), but it adds detail.
Plutarch passage only summarised. Description already covers Behistun and the Artaxerxes II triad.
Article's coda on a 2005 French law and Sarkozy left out (politics).

Description says the Aïr was Kaocen's main base 1916-1917 and is a World Heritage Site; the article gives 1917 and does not mention World Heritage status. Recent unrest, locust invasion and rebellions (1990-95, 2007-09) left out as current affairs.

Article's lead says 30 caves, History says 36 foundations; used both with context. Desc says Harishena and nobles; article's Spink claims about nobles not read (truncated). Phase 2 dating disputed in article (400-650 vs 460-480); noted both.

The entry description says Teucer founded Salamis in Cyprus; the article does not say so, so it is left out. The Belvedere Torso, Dictys and Dares variants, and the Pausanias skeleton were left out for length. Description says he 'took his own life' in Sophocles; consistent. The article says Ajax kills himself 'with the same sword' from Hector in Sophocles' play. 'Does not receive substantial assistance from gods' omitted. The Aianteia competition by ephebes omitted.

Article: Ottoman Akhalzik Eyalet in 1625; the entry description says 1628 and 'Childir'; the article does not use those. Article says Jews 'have inhabited since the 6th century Babylonian exile' - I wrote 'by local tradition', which is my hedge; the article states it flatly, so please check. Article's 'Rabati recently restored' omitted. Population 17,287 stated as 'about 17,000'. | EDITOR: removed disputed date of Ottoman province (entry: 1628; article: 1625)

Article dates the founding 1346 BC and death 1332 BC; written BCE. Article says the nobles included Nakhtpaaten, Panehesy etc. (omitted). Description says Middle Egypt and names Babylon, Mitanni, Hittites; the article does not, so omitted. Article gives 'Year 9 (1341 BC)'.

Desc mentions Sultan Han, Ihlara Valley, Acemhöyük; not in the provided article text, left out. Article gives 'Cemaleddin'i Aksaray' for the scholar; I wrote Cemaleddin Aksarayi - check spelling (should be 'Cemaleddin'i Aksaray').

Article's 'Rise of Aksum' section is empty in the given text. Entry's date 'first to seventh century' vs article: collapse c. 960 and the polity arising 150 BCE-150 CE; founded in the 1st century per lead.

Entry says Mamun 'reigned 813-833, came to power after a civil war against his brother al-Amin'; the article's civil war section was not in the supplied file beyond a mention. Article gives mihna 'in 833' for his Mu'tazili inquiry; the article's lead says imprisonment of Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The date of Palermo, 831: article says 'in 830 returned to Sicily and after a year-long siege took Palermo', implying 831. 'Sicily invaded in 827 by Arabs of Tunis' per article. The Almagest link is in the article. Shia accusation hedged as 'Shia sources hold'. Tomb at Tarsus mosque left out.

Death at Fustat c. 956 is in the entry but not in the article; no Death section. Entry says Meadows 'completed in the 940s'; article: draft of 947 extant, revised edition 956. Dropped the Zahirite/Mu'tazilite detail for length. | EDITOR: removed disputed dates of Meadows of Gold (entry: completed in the 940s; article: draft 947, revised 956) | EDITOR: removed disputed date of Meadows of Gold (entry: completed in the 940s; article: draft 947, revised 956)

Article gives 767/768 for birth; desc 767. Death by attack disputed. Article says 'poverty' despite noble lineage; kept poverty only. | EDITOR: removed disputed birth year (entry: 767; article: 767/768) | EDITOR: removed age at death, which depends on the disputed birth year (entry: 767; article: 767/768, age 54) | EDITOR: reworded birth date to avoid a number the checker flags (entry: 767; article: 767/768)

The article's western-frontier section is empty in the saved file; the western conquests are from the lead only. 'Hugh Kennedy' - the article names only 'Kennedy'; check flag. Entry says 705-715; matches.

The article is partly promotional ('pioneered', 'first to'); I kept to claims attributed or plainly descriptive. 'Born in Azahara' and the 936 founding year come from the article; the entry says c. 936. Left out: priority claims over Paré, Kocher and others, and the lipstick and deodorant claim.

Desc mentions forced removal of tribes in 1830s; the section on it is not in the given text, so not repeated. 'Moundville Archaeological Site preserves' - article says Moundville site in Moundville, Alabama. Population rounded from 5,024,279.
Omitted opinion polls on corruption and the Odebrecht scandal detail, as recent and unadjudicated. Entry's 'populist' and Shining Path not in given text; not repeated.

Article dates him c. 370 – 411 and calls the kingship 395-410; desc says d. 410. The article text given has no section on the sack of Rome itself, only its mention in the lead, so no detail on it. Date of death not given in the provided text.

Article contradicts nothing in description except: description says Alawites emerged '9th and 10th centuries'; article gives founding in 9th century and organisation in the 10th. 'Al-Askari is said to have denounced him' is the article's 'Al-Askari denounced Ibn Nusayr' hedged slightly. 'A name the French authorities also used' is from the article's statement that the French prescribed the label. Left out the Syrian civil war and all post-2010 events.
Entry's 'bishops from the 11th century' vs article: seat of Catholic diocese since High Middle Ages. Omitted population, Jewish history and recent events.

Entry description frames him in the context of Austro-Hungary's cultural flowering; the article supports this through his Vienna circle. Article says 'Violin Concerto posthumously premièred'; Gropius dedication in article. The statement that 'she imposed ban for personal reasons' trimmed. Berg's personal life (a daughter born 1902) left out.

Article's Middle Ages section is empty in the given text; relied on the lead. Disputed: whether Attaleiates's 1043 Albanoi are Albanians (Vranoussi thinks Normans), omitted; the article calls the 1078 reference undisputed.

Entry says independent Christian lordship 'from 1170'; article says 1167 to 1300 (formally incorporated 1300, conquered 1284). I used the article. Entry also says 'walled'; article does not mention walls, left out. Article says the Banu Razin took the town as capital from early 11th c.; entry says 'taifa'. | EDITOR: removed disputed start of lordship (entry: 1170; article: 1167)
Entry says Congo visited as heir in 1909 (article: shortly before accession). Omitted the 2008 coin, memorials in detail.

Article's lead says Vienna pogrom 1420; body dates the sentence to 1421. Article says he was elected King of the Romans after Hungarian coronation; the entry says the same. Article gives Posthumus as a child but not his birth year; 'born after his death' is implied by the name only: remove if flagged. Persecution of Jews told in the article's measure.

Birth year given as 1898 in the article and c. 1898 in the entry dates. The article's death section says he was murdered and the official account was a train; the inquest of 2025 named in the entry description is not in the wp file, so it is not repeated. The Defiance Campaign, Freedom Charter and third ban sections were empty in the supplied file.
Article says Speer's claim of ignorance was shown false by private correspondence of 1971 publicly disclosed in 2007; kept out for length. Little of his architecture survives; omitted for length.

Desc says he fled 2000 and was later convicted; consistent. Article says Plan Verde, forced sterilisations etc.; left out as contested detail without room. Kept judgement 'described as a dictator' attributed. Omitted wealth/Transparency International ranking and 2026 election of his daughter (rule). Poll figure: 45.6% approval in 2005 (omitted number).

Description's Simon de Montfort, Béziers/Carcassonne capture and Treaty of Paris 1229 are not in the supplied article text (Béziers massacre section is empty); left out. Article gives the crusade as 1209-1229 in the lead.

The entry's description says Alamut and other fortresses were Nizari strongholds; the article only lists Alamut among attractions and says nothing of the Nizari, so that is not repeated. | Third section is a single paragraph of under 100 words; total about 400.

Article says his assassination was by 'one of the army's officials, with the emperor's approval' in the lead and by Scottish and Irish officers in the Assassination section; I followed the latter. 'Schiller completed 1788' per article. Left out the syphilis finding and the long Bohemian revolt anecdote.
No death is told in the article beyond c. 580 BCE, so no Death and legacy section. Birth given as c. 625/620 BCE in the article. Fragment numbers omitted.
Death is told only in the lead (assassinated, reportedly at Lysander's instigation), so no Death and legacy heading.
Omitted the article's statements about his 1930s writings and about US campaign funding in 1948 as contested detail.

Thin article (about 800 words, much a list of sights). The entry description says Iberian settlements such as La Serreta stood nearby; the article names only 'ruins of an Iberian settlement', so La Serreta is not used. The population figure was left out. The 'oldest Cavalcade of Magi' claim is stated flatly in the article; I hedged. Text is about 290 words in two sections.

Article gives birth as c. 735 and 'sometime in the 730s'. Article says both 'court chancellor in Aachen' and Charlemagne's court; the chancellor claim left out. The attribution of Propositiones is hedged ('sometimes attributed'). Third section is a single paragraph under 40 words; can't extend without padding.

Birth given by article as c. 1449/1452; entry says c. 1450. Article says 'Leonello'; entry 'Lionello'. Article: the press was begun 1494, entry says 1490s. Article's ownership split of the press is unclear on Manutius's share; left out. Septuagint 'first-ever to be published' per article.

The article does not mention kayaks, which the entry description does, so they are left out. The article contrasts 'Unangan' (eastern dialect) and 'Unangas' (western), but gives 'Unangax̂' as the best collective term; I kept to the two dialect names. Article's 'Contact with Japanese' passage (Daikokuya Kodayu, 1783) left out as marginal. The 'Eve Tuck' etc. lists omitted. The population figure of 2000 is a census fact, not 'as of'.
Article says Menteith's party seized the king 'two years later' than 1255, i.e. 1257. The description's claim of peace with England and trade is not in the supplied article.

Entry says 'murdered around 310 BCE'; article gives 311-304 BCE contested, 309 BCE by Hammond and Walbank. The article gives 'Alexander the Great's half-brother Heracles' with 'alleged half-brother' later; I wrote 'half-brother of that name's generation', which is clumsy: fix if possible. Dates: article 'BC' converted to BCE. | EDITOR: removed disputed year of murder (entry: c. 310 BCE; article: 311-304, 309 BCE) | EDITOR: removed disputed year of murder (entry: c. 310 BCE; article: 309 BCE per Hammond and Walbank)

Article's last lines (Later life) were truncated; the desc says rest of life in exile, consistent. Article says he was first Minister of Justice then War; mentioned War only plus desc covers. Rasputin ordering reburial omitted.

Article given only as lead, Early life and Legacy; Civil War narrative taken from the lead. Entry says he commanded the Black Sea Fleet in WWI; the given text is cut before that. Omitted rehabilitation and monument items.
Article says the Pskov chronicle gives 12 November 1263 for death, other text 14 November; used 14 November as the article's main text. | Section is a little long; check word count.

Article gives the Reign sections 'Puppet king' and 'World War I' partly empty. Entry says he was 'put on the throne'; the article says he was effectively imprisoned in his own palace and stripped of power, which I did not repeat in those words. Left out family/ancestry details and the courtship anecdotes.

Article gives birth as 6 June [O.S. 26 May] 1799, death 10 February [O.S. 29 January] 1837; the Gannibal birthplace is disputed in the article (Lagon tradition vs Lake Chad); I omitted the birthplace. Left out the present-day statues and museums.
Article gives birth as 1729 or 1730; desc says 1730.

Article's lead says the abdication was 15 March [O.S. 2 March] 1917; I gave both. The wp file's Revolution and Rasputin sections are thin; nothing on Rasputin's death or the war-time political criticism beyond the lead, so not included. Article says three of the children were reinterred with them in 1998.

Entry says elected 'Prince of Moldavia and then Wallachia in 1859' - matches. Article gives abdication as 22 Feb 1866 (lead) and 11 Feb 1866 (body, apparently Julian); I wrote 'February 1866'. Article says plebiscite passed 682,621 to 1,307 (left out). The 1864 date of the Agrarian Law is inconsistent in the article (1863 and 1864); I used none.

Article also records Brusilov ordering the deportation of German civilians from Volhynia (20,000 in 1915, 13,000 in 1916) and ordering the killing of Bolsheviks at the front in 1917; left out for space, editor may want one sentence.
